title: RS_SetValue
description: >
  Returns the raster with one pixel of a band set to a new value.
kernels:
  - returns: raster
    args:
    - raster
    - name: col_x
      type: integer
      description: Column of the pixel (1-based).
    - name: row_y
      type: integer
      description: Row of the pixel (1-based).
    - name: new_value
      type: double
      description: The value to store.
  - returns: raster
    args:
    - raster
    - name: band
      type: integer
      description: >
        Band index (1-based). When omitted, the raster must have a single band;
        on a multiband raster the band has to be given.
    - name: col_x
      type: integer
      description: Column of the pixel (1-based).
    - name: row_y
      type: integer
      description: Row of the pixel (1-based).
    - name: new_value
      type: double
      description: The value to store.
---

## Description

`col_x` and `row_y` count from 1, as in Sedona Spark; note that the grid form
of `RS_Value` counts from 0. The pixel is overwritten even if it holds the
band's nodata value, and the band's nodata value is unchanged.

The value is stored in the band's pixel type: an integer band truncates it
toward zero (3.9 is stored as 3) and a float32 band rounds it to the nearest
float32. A value outside an integer band's range, NaN, a pixel outside the
grid, or a band the raster does not have is an error. Only 2-D rasters are
supported.

## Examples

```sql
SELECT RS_Value(RS_SetValue(RS_Example(), 1, 2, 2, 42), 1, 1, 1);
```
